research_rationale:
Executive Order 12235 (45 FR 58803, signed 1980-09-03) delegates to the Secretary of Energy the President's functions under sections 301 to 304(c) of the Natural Gas Policy Act of 1978 (15 U.S.C. 3361-3364(c)) and section 607 of the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 (15 U.S.C. 717z), keeping to the President the authority to declare, extend and terminate a natural gas supply emergency, and adds consultation, redelegation and cooperation commands. I read the complete held text (the text layer of the govinfo Federal Register page, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12235.txt; identity confirmed by the order number, title, date, FR Doc. 80-27464 line and the 45 FR 58803 page heading). The held text layer joins the tail of section 1-102 with sections 1-103 and 1-104 in the scope the inventory calls sec1-102-a; I decide that scope as one unit and state each of its parts in its reason. No clause has an own-terms end. The order's own authority is section 304(d) of the Natural Gas Policy Act, and the current text of 15 U.S.C. 3364(d) (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t15-s3364.txt, release point 119-121) still authorizes the President to delegate authority under sections 3361, 3362, 3363 and 3364 and to authorize redelegation. The same file prints Executive Order 12235 in its notes with no ending statement. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel prints the order in a note to 15 U.S.C. 3364 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09), and Table IV lists it there. The text of 15 U.S.C. 3361-3363 and 717z is not held; the claim does not rely on it beyond the cross-references in 15 U.S.C. 3364 (which still names sections 3361, 3362 and 3363) and on the point that the same release point marks repealed Code provisions with the word former (for example the note to 42 U.S.C. 5195 prints former 50 U.S.C. App. 2286(a)(4)) and does not do so for 15 U.S.C. 3361-3364 or 717z in this order's note; this is an inference from the editorial convention, not a finding that those sections are in force. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog and a search of the held texts for the order number found no amendment, revocation or supersession: the only other held text naming the order is the 1989 OFR codification, which prints it unamended. The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09, so laws enacted from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that search. The U.S. Code note and the extracted Code text named above are leads: their original release-point bytes are not held, so the current-law basis cited in this claim is the order's own held text read with the three bounded searches.
